overall: Conditions in Los Angeles early this morning show a current/running max of 64.4°F at 02:50 ET, which is effectively the overnight temperature rather than a meaningful daytime reading — peak heating is still roughly 12 hours away. The pattern is classic marine-influenced June gloom: patchy coastal fog, south winds, and a modest temperature ceiling. No tropical or severe weather concerns for the LA basin; the active wind advisories are confined to inland mountain and desert zones well away from the coast.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance has a moderate spread: ECMWF is the warmest at 73°F, HRRR at 71°F, and NBM at 67°F, with the official NWS forecast splitting the difference at a 'high near 70°F.' The INTRADAY model distribution is essentially uninformative at this pre-dawn hour (wide, flat tails into the 80s and 90s are an artifact of very limited warm-side observations) and should be discounted heavily; the META and D1_NOW models, which draw on NWP guidance, are far more credible at this stage.
max_temp_prediction: The META model — the most reliable fusion signal — concentrates 44.6% of probability in the 72–73°F bucket and another 32.6% in 74–75°F, implying a modal outcome just above the NWS 70°F call, likely in the 72–73°F range. The 13.8% META spike at 84–85°F appears to be residual INTRADAY model contamination and is inconsistent with all NWP guidance and the NWS narrative; it should be treated as noise. Given south onshore flow, fog clearing by midday, and a predicted peak near 14–16h ET, a daily high around 72°F is the best central estimate with moderate confidence — spread driven mainly by how quickly fog burns off and whether the onshore flow strengthens.
